Computer Vision III — Notes 3: Image Segmentation

Published 23 August 2026 · Updated 24 August 2026 · Course notes › Computer Vision › Computer Vision III · 261 words · 2 min read · views

We again build up from classical methods to deep learning. Segmentation begins as a grouping problem: superpixels and clustering — k-means, spectral clustering, mean shift — leading to normalized cuts, and then to energy-based models such as CRFs. Deep learning enters with the fully convolutional network (FCN) and 1×1 convolutions; the difficulties of dense pixel-level prediction are addressed by dilated convolutions and upsampling. From semantic segmentation we move to instance segmentation with Mask R-CNN, whose RoI rounding problem motivates coordinate-based networks such as PointRend. Panoptic segmentation unifies the two tasks — Panoptic FPN, Panoptic FCN, and how panoptic quality is evaluated. Finally, video object segmentation (VOS): one-shot (semi-supervised) versus zero-shot (unsupervised) settings; motion-based VOS built on optical flow (FlowNet, correlation layers, SegFlow); appearance-only VOS (OSVOS, OnAVOS, MaskTrack); and metric-based approaches that cast VOS as pixel-wise retrieval.
